title: When Cookery Became a Classroom Subject
paras: In nineteenth-century Britain, learning to cook gradually moved beyond watching an experienced relative. On a large country [[estate|estate]], a young kitchen worker might spend months washing vegetables before being allowed near a sauce. Such training produced skilled cooks, but offered little explanation of why particular methods worked.

The cookery schools that developed later in the century tried to make this knowledge teachable. Recipes became lessons with measured quantities: a British [[gallon|gallon]] of water, for instance, meant about 4.55 litres rather than an uncertain bucketful. Science entered the classroom too. Elementary chemistry explained that water contained [[hydrogen|hydrogen]] and oxygen, while practical demonstrations showed how slow cooking could make tough meat [[tender|tender]]. The aim was understanding, not simply obedience.

This approach reflected a broader educational ideal: the cook could be a [[thinker|thinker]] as well as a worker. Teachers drew on scientific [[findings|findings]] about food and heat, although some explanations were later corrected. Printed manuals, including [[best-selling|best-selling]] household guides, carried lessons beyond the classroom. Meanwhile, the [[administrative|administrative]] work of arranging ingredients, collecting fees and keeping accounts helped turn occasional demonstrations into regular courses.

The change was neither immediate nor complete. For beginners, a collapsed pudding could still seem an [[utter|utter]] disaster, whatever the textbook said. Yet written instructions allowed them to try again without waiting for an expert. Their [[gratitude|gratitude]] might be directed towards a patient teacher, but the lasting achievement was greater independence: kitchen knowledge could now be studied, questioned and shared.
zh: 在十九世纪的英国，学习烹饪逐渐不再局限于观察有经验的亲人操作。在一座大型乡间庄园里，年轻的厨房帮工可能要洗上几个月的蔬菜，才有机会接触酱汁制作。这种训练培养出了熟练的厨师，却很少解释某些方法为什么有效。
十九世纪后期兴起的烹饪学校试图让这些知识变得可以系统教授。食谱变成了用量明确的课程：例如，一英制加仑的水约为4.55升，而不是容量不明的一桶水。科学也进入了课堂。基础化学解释了水含有氢和氧，而实际演示则展示了慢炖如何使难嚼的肉变得软嫩。教学的目的是理解，而非一味照做。
这种方法体现了一种更广泛的教育理念：厨师不仅可以是劳动者，也可以是善于思考的人。教师借鉴有关食物和热的科学研究结果，不过其中一些解释后来得到了修正。印刷出版的手册，包括畅销的家政指南，将课程知识传播到了课堂之外。与此同时，采购安排、收费和记账等管理工作，帮助零星的演示活动发展成了定期开设的课程。
这种转变既非一蹴而就，也并不彻底。对初学者而言，无论教科书怎么说，一个塌掉的布丁仍可能意味着彻头彻尾的失败。然而，书面指导让他们不必等专家到场，就能再次尝试。他们或许会感激一位耐心的老师，但更持久的成果是独立能力的增强：厨房里的知识如今可以被学习、质疑和分享。

q.s: Traditional kitchen training could develop practical ability without explaining the reasons behind cooking techniques.
q.why: 首段指出传统训练培养技能，却少解释原理。

q.s: All the scientific explanations used by cookery teachers remained unchanged.
q.why: 第三段说明一些解释后来得到了修正。

q.s: Most beginners felt more grateful to their teachers than to the writers of cookery manuals.
q.why: 末段提及感激老师，但未比较两者。
